info.text: Unit 7 — Requesting parts from stores. Rich quiz, split by skill: Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary. CEFR B2.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Which part number does the technician give for the hydraulic filter?

generalfeedback.text: The technician reads it out as "two-six-one-one-four-five-zero-one" — 26114501. Reading back digits exactly is a core stores skill.

feedback.text: Correct — two-six-one-one-four-five-zero-one.
The last two digits are wrong — listen again to the end.
The middle digits are wrong — the order is 1-1-4-5.
Close, but the fourth and fifth digits are 1 and 4, not 4 and 0.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What does stores say will arrive with each filter?

generalfeedback.text: Stores says each filter "arrives with a serviceable tag and an EASA Form 1". A part is only fit to fit when it carries both.

answer.text: A serviceable tag and an EASA Form 1

feedback.text: Correct — the fitness tag plus the release certificate.

answer.text: A work order and a requisition number

feedback.text: These are job papers, not the papers that ship with the part.

answer.text: A batch record and a quarantine label sheet

feedback.text: A quarantine label marks a part you must not use — the opposite here.

answer.text: A shelf-life card and a delivery note

feedback.text: Not mentioned — listen for "serviceable tag" and "Form 1".

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. Why can stores not send the valve at once?

generalfeedback.text: Stores checks the shortage list and says the valve "is on backorder" — the stock is zero, so it must be ordered from the supplier.

feedback.text: Correct — the stock is zero and it waits on the supplier.

answer.text: It is being held in quarantine.

feedback.text: Quarantine is for a rejected part; the backorder is a stock issue.

answer.text: It has no valid serviceable tag.

feedback.text: The tag is not the problem here — the problem is zero stock.

answer.text: It failed the last leak test on the line.

feedback.text: That was the filter in Dialogue 1, not the valve in Dialogue 3.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. Stores says the stores list shows a different number because the original relay was superseded last year.

generalfeedback.text: True. Stores explains that "the original was superseded last year", which is why the shelf number differs from the work order.

feedback.text: Correct — the original part number was replaced by a newer one.
Listen again: stores says the original number was superseded last year.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many filter units does the technician request? (Write a figure.)

generalfeedback.text: The technician says "a quantity of two" — one to fit and one spare. Answer: 2.

feedback.text: Correct — two units.
Four is the number stores holds, not the number requested.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. What is the supplier's lead time, in days? (Write a figure.)

generalfeedback.text: Stores says "the lead time from the supplier is ten days". Answer: 10. (In the Dialogue 4 voicemail it is later cut to three.)

feedback.text: Correct — ten days, which is too long for an AOG.
Three days is the new lead time in the Dialogue 4 voicemail, not Dialogue 3.

questiontext.text:
Read this MEL entry.

MEL 29-11-01: One hydraulic filter may be deferred for up to 10 days, provided the second filter is serviceable and a daily check is carried out.

What condition allows the filter to be deferred?

generalfeedback.text: The MEL allows the deferral only provided the second filter is serviceable (and a daily check is done). "Provided" introduces the condition.

feedback.text: Correct — that is the condition after "provided".

answer.text: The supplier lead time is under ten days.

feedback.text: The ten days is the deferral limit, not a lead-time condition.

answer.text: A new work order has already been raised.

feedback.text: The entry says nothing about a work order.

answer.text: The aircraft is parked on the ground now.

feedback.text: Not stated — the condition is the second filter's status.

name.text: R2 · Reading · task card / IPC note

questiontext.text:
Read this task-card note.

Task card 24-31-00: Fit relay P/N 592011. Note: P/N 592011 supersedes P/N 592010. The two relays are interchangeable only when the aircraft is at mod 41 or above.

When are the two relays interchangeable?

generalfeedback.text: Interchangeability here depends on mod status: only at mod 41 or above. Below that standard, they are not interchangeable.

answer.text: At mod 41 or above on the aircraft.

feedback.text: Correct — the mod status must be 41 or higher.

answer.text: When the two batch numbers are identical.

feedback.text: The note says nothing about matching batch numbers.

answer.text: When the shelf life has not yet expired.

feedback.text: Shelf life is a different check; here it is the mod status.

answer.text: When stores holds both relays in stock.

feedback.text: Stock level does not decide interchangeability.

questiontext.text:
Read this Service Bulletin extract.

SB A320-32-1099: Operators should replace valve P/N 33078 with P/N 33079 at the next scheduled check. The replacement valve carries a valid EASA Form 1.

True or false: the bulletin states that the replacement valve has a valid EASA Form 1.

generalfeedback.text: True. The last sentence states the replacement valve "carries a valid EASA Form 1", so its certification status is in order.

feedback.text: Correct — the bulletin confirms a valid Form 1.
Read the last sentence again — it confirms a valid Form 1.

questiontext.text:
Read this tech-log entry.

Tech log: The unserviceable valve has been placed in quarantine. Do not refit. Await disposition from Quality.

True or false: the technician may refit the quarantined valve at once.

generalfeedback.text: False. The entry says "Do not refit" and to await disposition from Quality. A quarantined part must not be used.

feedback.text: No — the entry clearly says "Do not refit".
Correct — a quarantined part must not be refitted.

name.text: U1 · Use of English · order to request

questiontext.text:
Rewrite this bare order as a polite request. Begin with Could you or Would you.

Check the stock. → ______

generalfeedback.text: Model: Could you check the stock, please? Use the modal first, then the base verb — no "to", no "-s".

feedback.text: Correct — a polite request with could.
Correct — would works here too.
Start with "Could you" or "Would you" + the base verb "check".

name.text: U2 · Use of English · order to request

questiontext.text:
Rewrite as a polite request with Could you or Would you.

Send me two filters. → ______

generalfeedback.text: Model: Could you send me two filters, please? The base verb "send" follows the modal directly.

answer.text: Could you send me two filters*

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: Would you send me two filters*

feedback.text: Correct.
Use "Could/Would you send me two filters".

name.text: U3 · Use of English · vocabulary gap

questiontext.text:
Write the missing term.

The valve is on ______, because the stock is currently zero.

generalfeedback.text: backorder — an order that waits because the stock is zero.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct — "on backorder".
Zero stock, so the order waits — it is on backorder.

name.text: U4 · Use of English · vocabulary gap

questiontext.text:
Write the missing term (two words).

The time you must wait for a part to arrive is the ______.

generalfeedback.text: lead time — the wait for a part to arrive from the supplier.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
It is the lead time.

name.text: U5 · Use of English · correct the modal

questiontext.text:
Correct the grammar mistake and write the whole line.

Could you to confirm the Form 1? → ______

generalfeedback.text: Model: Could you confirm the Form 1? There is no "to" after a modal — use the base verb.

feedback.text: Correct — the "to" is removed.
Correct.
Remove "to": Could you confirm the Form 1?

questiontext.text:
Write the three-letter code.

The short code for "aircraft on ground" is ______.

generalfeedback.text: AOG — aircraft on ground; a missing part is stopping a flight, so the request is urgent.

feedback.text: Correct.
It is AOG.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: These are the core stores terms: a serviceable tag says a part is fit to fit; a Form 1 is the release certificate; quarantine locks away parts you must not use; interchangeability is whether two parts can swap safely; a requisition authorises you to take a part.

answer.text: a label that says a part is fit to fit
the EASA release certificate for a part
a locked area for parts you must not use
whether two parts can swap safely
a formal request to take a part from stores
the last date you may fit a part

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb or phrase it goes with.

generalfeedback.text: Word partners matter: you quote a part number, confirm a quantity, raise a requisition, check the IPC, and a part goes on backorder.

questiontext.text: Which term means "not fit to fit; you must not use it"?

generalfeedback.text: unserviceable means a part is not fit to fit. Its opposite, "serviceable", means it is fit.

feedback.text: Correct.
That means two parts can swap safely.
That is the opposite — fit to fit.
That is the place for bad parts, not the state of the part.

questiontext.text: Which term means "a locked area for parts you must not use"?

generalfeedback.text: quarantine is the restricted area where a rejected part is held until Quality clears it.

feedback.text: Correct.
That is an order waiting on zero stock.
That is a formal request for a part.
That is a link from one part number to another.
